verified_key_information_units.information: Revenue increased by EUR 1.4 million (2.4%) to EUR 59.3 million in H1 2026, with segment breakdowns of Passenger harbours (+2.9%), Cargo harbours (–2.5%), Ferry (+1.7%), and Other (+19.0%). Key drivers included higher charter fees from the icebreaker Botnica (EUR 0.9 million, +18.2%), increased electricity sales (EUR 0.6 million, +25.0%), and growth in ferry services revenue (EUR 0.3 million, +1.9%).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 6; KPI Table page 4; Segment Reporting tables pages 8-9

candidate_sentences.text: The Group generated revenue of EUR 59.3 million, representing a 2.4% increase compared to EUR 57.9 million in the same period of the previous year.
This growth was primarily driven by higher charter fees from the multifunctional icebreaker Botnica, increased revenue from the sale of electricity, and a rise in ferry service sales.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational volumes declined significantly: cargo handling fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes (mainly due to liquid bulk down 33.8%), passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million (with the Tallinn–Helsinki route down 2.6%), and vessel calls dropped 4.8%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section pages 4-6; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Operational volumes reflected a challenging market environment.
Total cargo handled decreased by 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, driven by a sharp 33.8% drop in liquid bulk volumes.
Passenger numbers fell by 2.0% to 3.6 million, although cruise passenger traffic surged by 47.8% due to an increase in cruise ship calls.
The number of vessel calls declined by 4.8%.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating expenses rose EUR 3.9 million (24.0%) in H1 2026, primarily from fuel costs up EUR 1.4 million (47.6%) due to higher prices and severe ice conditions, electricity costs up EUR 0.7 million (28.8%), and technical maintenance/repair expenses up EUR 1.2 million (80.0%).

candidate_sentences.text: However, these gains were insufficient to offset a significant surge in operating expenses, which rose by 24.0% to EUR 20.2 million.

The increase in costs was largely attributable to higher fuel prices, which pushed fuel expenses up by 47.6%, as well as increased electricity costs and higher expenditures on technical maintenance and repairs.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating profit decreased by EUR 4.7 million (25.7%) to EUR 13.6 million and profit for the period declined by EUR 4.3 million (41.7%) to EUR 6.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell EUR 4.0 million (13.5%) to EUR 25.8 million, mainly due to higher operating expenses, lower cargo/passenger volumes, and the absence of prior-year one-off gains (land sale profit and insurance indemnity).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 7-8; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Consequently, operating profit decreased by 25.7% to EUR 13.6 million, down from EUR 18.3 million in the prior year period.
Adjusted EBITDA also declined, falling by 13.5% to EUR 25.8 million from EUR 29.8 million.

The profit for the period was significantly impacted by the absence of one-off gains that had boosted the comparative period, specifically a EUR 0.9 million profit from the disposal of land for the Rail Baltica project and an insurance indemnity received for repair works on the icebreaker Botnica.
As a result, net profit for the six-month period dropped by 41.7% to EUR 6.0 million, with earnings per share decreasing to EUR 0.02 from EUR 0.04.

verified_key_information_units.information: Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (versus EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, upgrades to the quay at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (versus EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

As of 30 June 2026, total assets were EUR 615.0 million (down from EUR 622.1 million), loans and borrowings were EUR 173.4 million (stable), total liabilities were EUR 247.4 million (up from EUR 241.2 million), equity was EUR 367.7 million (down from EUR 380.9 million), and cash and cash equivalents were EUR 27.6 million (down from EUR 32.0 million).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Financial Position page 18

candidate_sentences.text: On the balance sheet, total assets decreased slightly by 1.1% to EUR 615.0 million, while equity declined by 0.3% to EUR 367.7 million.
Net debt increased by 1.5% to EUR 145.8 million, although total loans and borrowings decreased by 5.7% to EUR 173.4 million due to principal repayments.

verified_key_information_units.information: Significant Q2 2026 events: (a) Tallinn City Council adopted detailed plans for Terminal A and D areas; (b) Icebreaker Botnica completed a 20-day North Sea project; (c) A EUR 32 million unsecured loan agreement was signed with OP Corporate Bank; (d) Up to 485 additional Regula ferry trips were ordered for summer 2026; (e) A EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid (85% of 2025 profit).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Significant Events section pages 15-17; Dividends section page 14

candidate_sentences.text: The company maintained its dividend policy, paying EUR 19.2 million in dividends for the 2025 financial year.
The company also secured a new EUR 32 million loan facility to support general business purposes and ongoing investments.

verified_key_information_units.information: At 30 June 2026, market capitalisation was EUR 335.06 million (versus EUR 340.85 million at 31 December 2025). The share price closed at EUR 1.274 (versus EUR 1.296 at the start of 2026), with 22,559 shareholders (67.0% held by the Republic of Estonia).

details.completeness_justification: The candidate summary adequately covers the core material meaning of K1 (revenue growth drivers), K2 (operational volume declines), K3 (expense increases), K4 (profit declines and adjusted EBITDA), K6 (balance sheet changes), K7 (significant Q2 events including loan and dividend), but omits the core investment details of K5 and market capitalisation/share price data of K8. The omissions in K5 and K8 do not fundamentally alter the overall financial picture presented, hence the score is 'Generally yes'.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is internally coherent. It presents a consistent narrative of declining profitability despite modest revenue growth, with clear explanations linking revenue drivers to offsetting cost increases. All statements about financial performance (revenue, expenses, profit, margins) are logically connected and support the central thesis of margin pressure. Operational metrics (cargo, passengers, vessel calls) are presented as contextual factors without contradiction. Balance sheet changes are described factually. There are no self-contradictions, logical gaps, organizational issues, or unnecessary repetition. The summary forms a coherent whole that tells a clear story of performance trends and challenges.
